prerequisites: No prerequisites. Competencies taught in the basic modules of Computer Science and the advanced modules Software Engineering and Software Practicum are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: describe and explain the basic concepts of process-based and system-based virtual machines
describe the structure of virtual machines
develop components of process-based VMs (such as scheduler, garbage collection, just-in-time compiler)
explain the methods of system-based VMs (hypervisor, hardware emulation, hardware virtualization, paravirtualization)
present exemplary modern research in the field of VM technology
compare implementation approaches for programming language concepts (code transformation vs. VM support)

syllabus_topics: Process-based virtual machines for modern programming languages
Managed resources to reduce programmer complexity
System-based virtual machines providing a virtual environment for entire computer systems (hardware and operating system)
Sharing of multiple virtual machines on a physical machine
Separation of virtual resources like memory

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solutions for at least two exercise assignments
Oral examination (individual examination) or written exam

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments must be achieved, and solutions for at least two exercise assignments must be presented orally. Grading is based on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science program.
